title: Vulnerability scanning and reading the report without panicking

videos.script: A scanner hands you a report. Six findings, in red, against a library your project uses. {{report}} The first instinct is to panic. The second is to ignore it. Both are wrong. {{instinct}} Six lines turn out to be three advisories, each printed twice. {{three}} Each one names a flaw in the library, and the conditions it needs. You read them, and then you read your own code. {{reach}} None of the three is reachable. One upgrade closes all of them anyway. {{fix}} When a fix has to wait, the finding is accepted, by a person, with a reason and an end date. {{accept}} Then the gate goes in the pipeline, so that nothing rated high or critical ships open. {{gate}} And the same way of reading applies to a scan of the running site: risk, confidence, and how many places it was seen. {{dast}}
